children.name: Concept of Ratio and Equivalent Multipliers

tooltip_popover.title: Concept of Ratio and Equivalent Multipliers
tooltip_popover.content: A ratio compares two quantities of the same unit through division: a:b = a/b. Simplifying ratios requires dividing both antecedent and consequent by their Highest Common Factor (HCF). Proportional scaling requires multiplying or dividing all terms by a constant factor k.
tooltip_popover.example: Lemonade Recipe Scaling: Doubling lemon juice and water preserves taste because ratio 1:5 stays constant.

children.name: Proportion Laws and Unit Rate Applications

tooltip_popover.title: Proportion Laws and Unit Rate Applications
tooltip_popover.content: A proportion equates two ratios: a/b = c/d. Cross Product Property: Product of extremes equals product of means (a * d = b * c). Unit Rate Method: Calculates the value for 1 unit first before scaling to the required quantity.
tooltip_popover.example: Checking proportion: 4, 8, 12, 24 -> 4*24 = 96 and 8*12 = 96 -> forms a valid proportion.
